hoy.titular: Abel concedes the Brasileirão as Palmeiras turn to the cups; the Pincha keep working at City Bell

foto.alt: Coaching staff give instructions to two players during a training session at City Bell.

hoy.resumen: After losing 2-1 to Cruzeiro, Abel Ferreira said the Brasileirão title "has been handed over" and complained of having only three days to prepare for the final. Estudiantes train at City Bell until Wednesday 25th, when they fly to Montevideo, and there is still no definitive medical update on Correa.

siete.titulo: Abel: "The title has been handed over"
siete.texto: After the 2-1 defeat at the Mineirão, the Palmeiras coach conceded the Brasileirão and congratulated Flamengo. He was without Gustavo Gómez and Maurício (back late from Paraguay duty) and still has Murilo, Jefté, Paulinho and Piquerez injured.

siete.titulo: Three matches in a week for Palmeiras
siete.texto: On Saturday 21st they host Flamengo, who can clinch the title, and on Tuesday 24th they visit Chapecoense in Chapecó at 18:00. Abel complained he will have just three days to prepare for the final at the Centenario.

siete.titulo: Correa a doubt for the final
siete.texto: He is still being treated for a grade 2 tear in his right hamstring and there is no definitive medical update yet. The coaching staff see him as an important attacking option, but his involvement at the Centenario is not guaranteed.

siete.titulo: Rojo, Palacios and Mancuso back with the group
siete.texto: Marcos Rojo, Tomás Palacios and Eros Mancuso started the week with gym work but are now training normally with the rest of the squad.

siete.titulo: The road map to the Centenario
siete.texto: Today there is training and a squad barbecue at City Bell. The players train there until Wednesday 25th (Sunday is a day off) and fly to Montevideo that afternoon, staying at the Hilton; on Thursday and Friday they will train at Montevideo City Torque's facilities.

siete.titulo: Without Baltasar, Medina weighs a back five
siete.texto: Baltasar Rodríguez, sent off against Flamengo at the Maracanã, will miss the final. According to El Día, the coach is considering five defenders at the Centenario to stop Palmeiras' full-backs getting forward.

siete.titulo: Around 35,000 Pincha fans head for Montevideo
siete.texto: 120 coaches are going: 60 laid on by the club, leaving the UNO on Friday afternoon, and 60 from supporters' groups and branches. Friday and Saturday ferries are sold out, and 2009 champions invited by the club will also be at the Centenario.

linea.texto: Abel Ferreira after the Cruzeiro defeat: "The title has been handed over".
Palmeiras lost at the Mineirão and Flaco López played his second match in two days.
Day by day, the squad's schedule up to the final: City Bell, travel on Wednesday 25th and training in Montevideo.
Total frenzy: 120 coaches, sold-out ferries and around 35,000 Pincha fans expected in Montevideo.
Giay, Flaco López and Arias came back injury-free from the international break and are available for Palmeiras against Cruzeiro.
The squad press on with their preparations for the final in Montevideo.
Cruzeiro and Palmeiras, second in the Brasileirão, meet today at the Mineirão with Verdão badly depleted.
Abel hit out at the fixture list: Palmeiras play in Chapecó on Tuesday 24th and will have three days to prepare for the final.
The women's team unveiled Mauro Silva as new head coach and a project running to 2030.
Jesús Valenzuela will referee the final between Estudiantes and Palmeiras at the Centenario.
The 1,000 extra seats for the final sold out in under an hour, amid website crashes and complaints.
Palmeiras wrapped up preparations for their trip to Cruzeiro with five absentees, Piquerez among them.
Palmeiras wrapped up preparations for Cruzeiro without their internationals: Murilo and Jefté target the final.
CONMEBOL opened an extra seat sale for the final, only for Banco Provincia Mastercard holders.
